blocks.html: Clients (classes or modules that use an interface) should not be forced to depend on methods they do not use.
blocks.text: Clients (classes or modules that use an interface) should not be forced to depend on methods they do not use.

blocks.html: Interfaces (contracts that define available methods) should be specific to client needs rather than large, general-purpose contracts.
blocks.text: Interfaces (contracts that define available methods) should be specific to client needs rather than large, general-purpose contracts.

blocks.html: Smaller, more focused interfaces reduce unnecessary dependencies and implementation burden.
blocks.text: Smaller, more focused interfaces reduce unnecessary dependencies and implementation burden.

blocks.html: Prevents “fat interfaces” that become dumping grounds for unrelated functionality.
blocks.text: Prevents “fat interfaces” that become dumping grounds for unrelated functionality.

blocks.html: Reduces unnecessary coupling between clients and unrelated features.
blocks.text: Reduces unnecessary coupling between clients and unrelated features.

blocks.html: Makes implementations simpler and more reliable by removing irrelevant requirements.
blocks.text: Makes implementations simpler and more reliable by removing irrelevant requirements.

blocks.html: Allows independent evolution of different parts of a system.
blocks.text: Allows independent evolution of different parts of a system.

blocks.html: Improves readability and maintainability of contracts.
blocks.text: Improves readability and maintainability of contracts.

blocks.html: Split one large interface into multiple role-specific interfaces.
blocks.text: Split one large interface into multiple role-specific interfaces.

blocks.html: Each client/implementation now depends only on the contracts it needs.
blocks.text: Each client/implementation now depends only on the contracts it needs.

blocks.html: No unnecessary method stubs or runtime errors for unsupported features.
blocks.text: No unnecessary method stubs or runtime errors for unsupported features.

blocks.html: How to check if the code follows ISP
blocks.text: How to check if the code follows ISP

blocks.html: Rule 1 — No Unused Methods in Implementations
blocks.text: Rule 1 — No Unused Methods in Implementations

blocks.html: Implementations should not have to provide empty or error-throwing methods.
blocks.text: Implementations should not have to provide empty or error-throwing methods.

blocks.html: Check: Review all classes implementing an interface. If any methods are unused or always throw, ISP is violated.
blocks.text: Check: Review all classes implementing an interface. If any methods are unused or always throw, ISP is violated.

blocks.html: Rule 2 — Interface Size Minimalism
blocks.text: Rule 2 — Interface Size Minimalism

blocks.html: Interfaces should contain the smallest possible set of methods to define a role.
blocks.text: Interfaces should contain the smallest possible set of methods to define a role.

blocks.html: Check: If removing a method from an interface would not break some implementers, the interface is too large.
blocks.text: Check: If removing a method from an interface would not break some implementers, the interface is too large.

blocks.html: Rule 3 — Client-Specific Contracts
blocks.text: Rule 3 — Client-Specific Contracts

blocks.html: Each interface should be shaped around the needs of a particular client or role.
blocks.text: Each interface should be shaped around the needs of a particular client or role.

blocks.html: Check: Identify the primary consumers of the interface. If multiple unrelated clients use only parts of it, ISP is violated.
blocks.text: Check: Identify the primary consumers of the interface. If multiple unrelated clients use only parts of it, ISP is violated.

blocks.html: Rule 4 — No Forced Methods
blocks.text: Rule 4 — No Forced Methods

blocks.html: A class should not be forced to provide methods it doesn’t actually need or use.
blocks.text: A class should not be forced to provide methods it doesn’t actually need or use.

blocks.html: Check: Look for methods that are empty, throw errors, or act as placeholders. If you find them, the Interface Segregation Principle is being broken.
blocks.text: Check: Look for methods that are empty, throw errors, or act as placeholders. If you find them, the Interface Segregation Principle is being broken.

blocks.html: Rule 5 — No “God Interfaces”
blocks.text: Rule 5 — No “God Interfaces”

blocks.html: Avoid one-size-fits-all interfaces for a broad range of functionalities.
blocks.text: Avoid one-size-fits-all interfaces for a broad range of functionalities.

blocks.html: Check: If the interface methods naturally group into separate responsibilities, split it.
blocks.text: Check: If the interface methods naturally group into separate responsibilities, split it.

blocks.html: Rule 6 — Independent Evolution
blocks.text: Rule 6 — Independent Evolution

blocks.html: Interface changes should affect only relevant implementations.
blocks.text: Interface changes should affect only relevant implementations.

blocks.html: Check: When a method is added, if unrelated classes must change, ISP is violated.
blocks.text: Check: When a method is added, if unrelated classes must change, ISP is violated.

blocks.html: Rule 7 — Dependency Clarity
blocks.text: Rule 7 — Dependency Clarity

blocks.html: Client code should only import and depend on the interfaces relevant to it.
blocks.text: Client code should only import and depend on the interfaces relevant to it.

blocks.html: Check: If a client has to reference an interface and ignore any of its methods, ISP is violated.
blocks.text: Check: If a client has to reference an interface and ignore any of its methods, ISP is violated.
